Based on `doc.txt`, here is what the document says about hunger and thirst during a fast:

**Hunger**
- "Fasting decreases hunger hormones and increases fullness. So although you may feel hungry when you first try fasting, many people actually report reduced hunger once they are used to it." (doc.txt)
- "You may struggle at first if you are not used to going for extended periods of time without food, but much of this could be down to habit." (doc.txt)
- "Most people adapt quite quickly though, so find it increasingly easy to fast." (doc.txt)
- "Dehydration can also be mistaken for hunger, which can make it more difficult to stick to your planned fast." (doc.txt)

**Thirst / hydration**
- "When you eat, you get some water from your food. So during a fast, you are missing out on some of the fluids you normally get. This can lead to you becoming dehydrated, causing side effects such as tiredness and headaches." (doc.txt)
- "The best option for staying hydrated is water." (doc.txt)

So the document says you may feel hungrier at first but that hunger tends to decrease as you get used to fasting, and that you can become dehydrated (and thus thirstier) because you miss the water you normally get from food.
